research_rationale:
Identity and text: the order was read in full in the registered Federal Register original (6 FR 1517, issue of 1941-03-20, PDF page 1; grade original_representation_unverified, acceptable_as_original true). Number 8714 is printed in the bracket after the signature, signed March 18, 1941, title 'Designating Certain Officers To Act as Secretary of the Treasury in Case of Absence or Sickness of the Secretary', agreeing with the census register row. Inventory: one sole paragraph with three succession designations (Fiscal Assistant Secretary; senior Assistant Secretary on duty; General Counsel) and a revocation of Executive Order No. 6202-B. End: Executive Order 10586, signed January 13, 1955 (20 FR 361, issue of 1955-01-15, held), orders that EO 8714 of March 18, 1941 "is hereby revoked", naming it by number, date and title. The dossier also lists EO 10588 as a revoking order; that record comes from the same Federal Register page extract, which prints EOs 10586, 10587 and 10588 one after another, and EO 10588 (President's Commission on Veterans' Pensions) does not mention EO 8714, so it is neither an end nor a later event. Held evidence only; the order is a NO.

operative_clauses.judgment_reason: Terminated by express revocation. EO 9830, Part III, revokes the listed Executive orders including "No. 8937 of November 7, 1941." The enacting clause orders EO 9830 "it is hereby ordered as follows, effective May 1, 1947:" so the end is recorded as 1947-05-01. Part III has no separate date and the enacting clause orders Parts I, II and III alike 'effective May 1, 1947'; the alternative reading is that the revocation took effect on signing, 1947-02-24 (printed 12 FR 1259, 1947-02-25). Later event (amendment, clause continues as amended): EO 9579 restated the proviso, effective as of December 8, 1944 ("This order shall be effective as of December 8, 1944."). Before: "Provided, that such persons shall notify the Civil Service Commission within forty days after their service in the armed forces has terminated that they desire to have the benefits of this order." After: "Provided, That such persons shall notify the Civil Service Commission within 90 days after termination of their service in the armed forces or of hospitalization continuing after discharge for a period of not more than one year." The change lengthens the notice period and adds hospitalization; the substance of the proviso changed.
